phase_0.boundary_condition: The single interface where local emission terminates without network propagation

⊢.justification: The state before the distinction of 'out' is made; the unmarked surface where no direction exists.

⊣.justification: The closed boundary that contains the emission event; the single point where the local scope ends.

≻.justification: The directed transformation from the internal state toward the exterior interface.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism that tests if the emission can be retracted or if it has crossed the boundary irreversibly.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of the emission event to the boundary condition.

⊙.justification: The recognition that the 'out' primitive is defined by its own termination; the element is itself.

∈.justification: Splits the emission into the affirmative path (successful exit) and the negative path (blocked or internal reflection).

∋.justification: Rejoins the exit and reflection arms into a single state describing the interface status.

⊤.justification: The constructive proof that the signal has crossed the interface and terminated externally.

⊥.justification: The constructive refutation of exit; the signal remains internal or is rejected by the boundary.

⊞.justification: The state where the signal is simultaneously exiting and reflecting, held at the interface without resolution.

⊡.justification: The permanent, append-only record of the emission event at the interface.

phase_3.both_description: The signal is simultaneously exiting and reflecting; the interface holds a contradiction of direction.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the pre-emission void where no direction exists.
Generate the emission vector directed toward the exterior.
Fork the emission into the path of successful exit and the path of internal reflection.
Evaluate the affirmative arm where the signal crosses the interface.
Chain the successful exit to the external termination point.
Record the successful emission as a permanent event.
Evaluate the negative arm where the signal is reflected or blocked.
Apply the reverse morphism to test the retraction of the reflected signal.
Hold the state where the signal is both exiting and reflecting at the boundary.
Rejoin the exit and reflection arms into a single boundary verdict.
Recognize the 'out' primitive as self-referential, defined by its own termination.
Anchor the system at the closed interface boundary.
